findings.title: Loss of precision when converting rounded cents to euros
findings.body: `toCents` expects an amount in euros, but the code passes `rounded` (a whole number of cents) instead. This converts cents back to euros, losing the cent-level precision the function was meant to preserve. Pass the original euro amount to `toCents` or refactor to work entirely in cents.

findings.title: Floating-point arithmetic used for money
findings.body: The calculation `totalCents(booking) * (percent / 100)` performs floating-point arithmetic on monetary values. This can introduce rounding errors. Perform the calculation in integer arithmetic (e.g., using basis points) or use a fixed-point library to avoid precision loss.

summary.problem: The new `depositCents` function introduces precision loss and uses floating-point arithmetic for money calculations.
summary.done_well: The function is clearly named and uses existing utilities (`totalCents`, `toCents`) to compute the deposit amount.
